title: Chemical and spot testing
audience: Carpet and upholstery cleaners who test products before using them on the item.
referencesAtStart: Official sources: Safe Work Australia, Hazardous chemicals register (no date shown); Safe Work Australia, Understanding safety data sheets for hazardous chemicals (no date shown in the text read); WorkSafe Victoria, The hierarchy of control (reviewed 30 July 2022).
learningOutcomes: Carry out a chemical and spot test on an inconspicuous area before the main treatment.
Read a test result for colour change, fibre damage, residue and bleed.
Never mix products and never test an unidentified product.

instruction.heading: Why test, and where
instruction.body: A test shows how the fibre and the dye react to a product before the whole item is treated. It is the only practical way to learn whether a dye will move, whether a fibre will mark, or whether a residue will form, and it is done even on familiar fabrics, because the same fibre can be dyed differently by two makers. Choose an inconspicuous area, such as the back of a corner, a hidden edge, the underside of a cushion or an area under furniture where the customer allows it. Where the item has several colours or several fibre types, test each one, because a test on one colour says nothing about another. The number of test spots is set by the item; for example, one spot per colour zone is a reasonable working approach (example only). The test must use the same product, the same dilution and the same method that will be used on the main area. A test with a weaker product is not a valid test of a stronger one.

instruction.heading: Carrying out the test
instruction.body: Prepare the test area in the way the planned method would prepare the main area, and apply the product as the method would apply it. Leave the product for the dwell time stated on its label, and do not extend the time to get a stronger result. Blot the area with a white cloth if the method calls for it. Allow the test area to dry fully, because a damp area can look different from a dry one, and judge the result only then. Keep the test spot unaffected by other work during the drying period, so that the result is not confused by a second product or by traffic. Photograph the test spot, with permission, before and after drying.

instruction.heading: Reading the result
instruction.body: Read the result against an untouched area in the same light. Look for colour change, which can be a lightening, a darkening or a shift in shade. Press a white cloth onto the test area and look for bleed, which shows as colour transfer. Look for fibre damage, such as fuzzing, fraying, crushing or a dull, stripped look. Feel for stiffness, which shows the product has affected the fibre or the backing. Look for residue and tide marks, which show as a ring or a film where the product dried. A result that shows any of these means the product or method is not suitable for the main area. A slight change that the customer has accepted in writing can be recorded as a limit, but a bleed or a fibre damage result is a stop.

instruction.heading: What to do when the test fails
instruction.body: Stop. Do not use the product on the main area, and do not try a stronger version of the same product. Record the product, the dilution, the test area, the method, the time and the result, with a photograph taken with permission. Choose a different approved method, test it in the same way, and check the new result. If no method passes, refer the item for a specialist assessment, and tell the customer what the test showed and what the next step is. A failed test is not a failure of the business; a treatment carried out after a failed test is.

instruction.heading: Products, mixing and safety data
instruction.body: Use one approved product at a time. Never mix products, because two products can react with each other and the result is not predictable. Never test or use a product from an unlabelled container, because the hazards and the directions are not known. Each product on the job needs a current safety data sheet, and the supplier can provide one at no cost on first supply or on request. A safety data sheet has 16 headings, including hazards, first aid, handling and storage, exposure controls and disposal, and it should have been prepared within the last five years (Safe Work Australia, fetched 2026-11-03). Each hazardous chemical on the workplace register is matched to a current safety data sheet, and the register is kept where workers can reach it.

instruction.heading: Records and the customer conversation
instruction.body: Record each test as a separate entry: the product, the dilution, the area tested, the time the product was left, the drying time, the result and any photographs. Record what was explained to the customer and what the customer agreed. Where a test leaves a visible but acceptable change, the customer's written agreement is part of the record. A test record that shows the reasons for a decision protects the business if the result is questioned later.

procedure: Choose an inconspicuous area, and the same product, dilution and method that are planned for the main area.
Prepare and apply the test as the planned method would, and leave the product for the label's stated time.
Allow the test area to dry fully, and keep it clear of other work and traffic while it dries.
Check for colour change, bleed on a white cloth, fibre damage, stiffness, residue and tide marks, comparing with an untouched area in the same light.
If the test shows a problem, stop, do not use the product on the main area, and choose a different approved method to test again.
Record the product, dilution, test area, timing, drying time, result and photographs, and record the customer's agreement.

workedExamples.situation: A test on a coloured upholstery panel, carried out on a hidden seam allowance, shows the dye bleeding onto a white cloth.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the product, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not use the product on the main panel. Record the bleed, the product, the dilution, the test area and the time. Photograph the cloth and the test area, with permission. Choose a different approved method that suits a dye that moves, test it in the same way, and check the new result on a white cloth. Agree the outcome with the customer, and explain that the first product was not used because of the bleed.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) After a test on a carpet edge, a pale ring has formed where the product dried. The ring was not present before the test.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the ring acceptable, and what do you do next?
workedExamples.reasoning: Treat the ring as a residue result. Do not use the product on the main area, and do not try to remove the ring with a second product. Record the ring, the product, the dilution and the removal method, if any, that the label gives. Test a different approved product or method with a clean rinse, check the result after it dries, and record it. If the ring is still present after the rinse, the method is not suitable for the item.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) A customer asks you to mix two products to get a stronger result on a stubborn mark on a fabric chair, to save time.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Do not mix products. Explain that two products can react and that the result cannot be predicted. Test one approved product on an inconspicuous area, record the result, and propose a further approved step only if the first result allows it. Record the request and the refusal.

equipmentAndPpe: White test cloth, for bleed checks
Approved products, each with its label and a current safety data sheet
Gloves and eye protection as set by the safety data sheet
Ventilation or a well-ventilated space, where the safety data sheet calls for it
Timer for the label's stated time
Test record sheet and camera or phone, used with permission

commonErrors.error: Skipping the test on a familiar fabric.
commonErrors.prevention: Test each item, including familiar ones, because two items of the same fibre can be dyed differently.

commonErrors.error: Judging the test while it is still wet.
commonErrors.prevention: Allow the test to dry fully, and compare it with an untouched area in the same light.

commonErrors.error: Mixing two products to get a stronger result.
commonErrors.prevention: Use one approved product at a time, and never mix products.

commonErrors.error: Using a product from an unlabelled container, or without a safety data sheet.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only labelled products, with a current safety data sheet on file.

commonErrors.error: Using the product on the main area after a bleed or residue result.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, record the result, and choose a different approved method to test again.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Each hazardous chemical on the workplace register is matched to a current safety data sheet, and the register must be kept where workers can reach it (Safe Work Australia, Hazardous chemicals register, fetched 2026-11-03; no date shown).

A safety data sheet has 16 headings, and the supplier can provide a copy at no cost on request. It should have been prepared within the last five years (Safe Work Australia, Understanding safety data sheets, fetched 2026-11-03).

The hierarchy of control places personal protective equipment last, as the weakest option, so the test is run with ventilation and the other controls first and PPE as the last layer (WorkSafe Victoria, reviewed 30/07/2022).
Do not treat the examples here as product instructions.
No Australian standard for carpet or upholstery spot testing was confirmed.

qualityStandard: The test is completed on an inconspicuous area with the planned product, dilution and method, in the practical.
A bleed or fibre damage result is identified and the product is rejected, in the case study.
Each result is recorded with the product, dilution, area, drying time and the decision taken.
No products are mixed and no unlabelled product is used, in the practical and the case study.
documentationEvidence: Test record with product, dilution, area, time, drying time and result
Rejection record for any product that fails the test
Photographs of the test area before and after drying, taken with permission
Record of the customer's agreement to any visible change that is accepted
summary: Test on an inconspicuous area with the planned product, dilution and method.
Judge the result only after the test area has dried fully.
Stop on any bleed, fibre damage or residue result, and choose a different approved method.
Never mix products, and never test or use one without a label and a current safety data sheet.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should a spot test be done?
options: In the middle of the main panel, where the stain is most likely to show
On the most visible spot, so the result can be judged quickly by the owner
On an inconspicuous area, such as a hidden edge or the underside of a cushion

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the test judged?
options: Straight away while it is still wet
After the test area has dried fully
Never, because the result is always fine

knowledgeChecks.question: The test shows dye bleed onto a white cloth. What is correct?
options: Use the product on the main panel, since the bleed is only light and will fade
Do not use it, record the result, and choose a different approved method
Mix in another product to fix the bleed, then test the main panel again

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks you to mix two products for a stronger result. What is correct?
options: Mix them if the customer signs a form
Refuse, use one approved product at a time, and record the request
Mix them in a small amount first and then use them on the main area
